subject: Integration follow-up: SDK auth & private access plan
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@cloudlink.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Integration follow-up: SDK auth & private access plan

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we stay aligned.

Key takeaways from our side:
- Primary integration path: Redwood hosted SDK + optional on-prem Private connector for inference (customer prefers VPC peering or private egress).
- Auth: Customer will use mTLS mutual auth for the private connector; fallback to API key with IP allowlist for hosted SDK traffic.
- Routing: Traffic from CloudLink staging should go to our Dedicated region-us-east-1 pool. Production will use Dedicated with canary routing.
- Features requested: embeddings + reranker for search ranking pipeline; structured tool-calling for invoice generation.

Open questions for CloudLink:
1) Do you have a preferred Egress model? (NAT egress, proxy, or VPC endpoint to our service?)
2) Will you manage certificate lifecycle in your KMS/HSM for mTLS, or want Redwood-managed certs?
3) Any restrictions on outbound DNS resolution from your VPC (we asked about split-horizon)?

Next steps (owners & dates):
- Alex: confirm preferred egress pattern and whether CloudLink will manage certs (by 2027-03-24).
- Marissa: share detailed security checklist and sample network diagram (I attached a sketch).
- Olga: schedule technical deep-dive for routing and embeddings tuning (propose Mar 25 or 26).

Attachments: redwood-network-sketch.pdf (high-level network sketch), auth-reqs-2027.xlsx (initial auth mapping)

Thanks — happy to jump on another call with your infra/security folks if helpful.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0197

---
Redwood Inference | Developer-first inference runtime
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@cloudlink.io>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@cloudlink.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration follow-up: SDK auth & private access plan

Thanks Olga — great summary. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing with infra: 

- Egress: we prefer to avoid NAT for production; we'd like either VPC endpoint (private link style) into Redwood or a dedicated egress proxy in our VPC that forwards to Redwood Dedicated.
- Certs: CloudLink prefers to manage certs (we can issue client certs from our internal PKI) but would like Redwood's requirements (acceptable algorithms, rotation window) documented.
- DNS: we do have split-horizon DNS for internal service names; outbound resolution to external hostnames is allowed but goes through our resolver.

On embeddings/rerank: our ML infra team asked about tokenization consistency and embedding dimension compatibility (we use 1024-d). Can you confirm Redwood's embedding models and whether we can pin dimension/quantization?

We can do the technical deep-dive on Thu Mar 25 10:00 AM PT. I'll invite our infra lead (Priya) and ML infra engineer.

Alex
Principal Engineer, CloudLink
alex.morgan@cloudlink.io

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration follow-up: SDK auth & private access plan

Alex / Priya — looping in our security and network pack for the upcoming deep-dive. A couple of quick pointers ahead of the call: 

1) Embeddings: we currently publish model dims in the catalog; our "redwood-embed-1024" variant is 1024-d and matches your expectation. We'll provide a pinned model id for determinism and a small eval prompt set to check parity.

2) mTLS certs: if CloudLink will manage client certs, Redwood supports verifying client cert CN and chain; required ciphers: TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 or better. Rotation cadence: we recommend 90 days; we can accept shorter windows.

3) VPC endpoint option: we provide a Private Endpoint appliance model (VPN-less) — it accepts inbound connections over a private link; we need the following from your side pre-call:
   - A list of source IPs for allowlist (we'll accept a /32 or CIDR).
   - DNS entry you want resolved internally -> our endpoint (we can support split-horizon DNS CNAME to our endpoint).
   - Egress path for the private connector (we need to know whether you will NAT or route directly).

Attached: our initial network sketch and auth matrix (same as Olga's). Also adding a short checklist for the call.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-network-sketch.pdf; auth-reqs-2027.xlsx
